# video_processor: system generation prompt

*Generated by `ip/scripts/make_ip_prompts.py` from the design sources on 2026-10-11. It follows `ip/docs/SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.md`; edit any field before use.*

```text
Create a complete FPGA / ASIC system for the FPGA Cores 4 U digital IP library, built from the
existing library IP wherever possible.
```

## 1. Identity and goal

- Top module: `video_processor`
- Location: `digital_ip/image_processing/video_processor/`
- Purpose: Top level of the video processing system (see docs/system_block_diagram.svg).
- Target: not selected (technology independent); vendor parts outside the top.

## 2. Features

- `VP_CSI2_RX`: MIPI CSI-2 camera input (D-PHY RX lanes, byte_clk). Without it the pipeline has no video source; the outputs can still show the test pattern.
- `VP_HDMI`: HDMI / DVI output (TMDS symbols)
- `VP_LVDS`: LVDS panel output (OpenLDI 7:1 words)
- `VP_DSI`: MIPI DSI panel output (D-PHY TX lanes)
- `VP_CSI2_TX`: MIPI CSI-2 output to a processor (D-PHY TX lanes)
- `VP_VISION`: vision_system lens-distortion correction at the video_pipeline insert point (implies VP_INSERT)
- `VP_FILTER`: blur_sharpen (blur / sharpen, 4 modes) in the insert loop, after vision_system (implies VP_INSERT)
- `VP_TRACK`: object_tracker (target search / measurement) and symbol_overlay (boxes, crosshairs) at the end of the insert loop, after blur_sharpen (implies VP_INSERT)
- `VP_INSERT`: video_pipeline insert point only (looped back here)

## 6. Architecture and behaviour

Implement this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
Top level of the video processing system (see
docs/system_block_diagram.svg). Version 2.0.0. Technology independent:
no target device is selected; a board wrapper adds the vendor D-PHY
RX / TX, differential buffers and I/O pads. All clocks except the
camera byte clock are generated inside from one board reference clock.

  u_cpu        py_soc           CPU system: clock generator (clk_gen,
                                two digital PLLs: every clock of the
                                design from ref_clk), Python bytecode
                                CPU booting from SPI flash, 2x UART,
                                2x I2C, 2x SPI, 96 GPIO, intc, watchdog;
                                external window 0x1_0000-0x1_FFFF ->
                                video registers
  u_axil_cdc   axi4_lite_cdc    cpu_clk -> pix_clk
  u_vbus       py_axil_xbar     video register bus (axi4_lite_decoder)
  u_pipe       video_pipeline   CSI-2 RX -> ISP -> [insert] -> scaler ->
                                timing -> hdmi_tx / lvds_tx / dsi_tx /
                                csi2_tx
  u_vs_adapt   vs_stream_adapter frame admission, line gaps, return
                                FIFO (vision_system output never stalls)
  u_vision     vision_system    lens-distortion correction at the
                                video_pipeline insert point (CTRL[7])
  u_filter     blur_sharpen     blur / sharpen after vision_system, same
                                insert loop (MODE 0-3, 4 = pass-through)
  u_track      object_tracker   target search: bounding box of the object
                                pixels in a search window, per frame, for
                                the CPU's tracking loop (passive tap after
                                blur_sharpen)
  u_overlay    symbol_overlay   boxes / crosshairs drawn over the video
                                (the tracked target: dashed box), last in
                                the insert loop
  u_frame_cnt  frame_counter    frames out of the first pipeline stage
                                (csi2_raw_unpack) and into the last one
                                (axis_to_video): end-of-frame interrupts
                                13 / 14 (bit_sync to cpu_clk) and their
                                counts; plus frames into and out of
                                vision_system and measured by
                                object_tracker; every marker time
                                stamped (us) in its event log, so the CPU
                                reports them in the order they happened
  u_irq_stats  pulse_sync       isp_stats frame done -> intc source 12
  u_tmds_ser   tmds_serializer  10:1 HDMI / DVI
  u_lvds_ser_a/b lvds_serializer 7:1 LVDS links A / B
  u_rst_*      reset_sync       one per core clock domain, all from the
                                CPU system's core reset output only
                                (the CPU clock domain reset comes from
                                py_soc, released once its PLL locks)

CPU address map (py_soc, mem32[] in the firmware):
  0x0_0100-0x0_C1FF  py_soc peripherals (see py_soc.sv)
  0x1_0000-0x1_7FFF  video_pipeline (0x1_4000+ scaler)
  0x1_8000-0x1_80FF  vision_system (axi_lite_regs)          `VP_VISION
  0x1_8200-0x1_83FF  blur_sharpen                           `VP_FILTER
  0x1_8400-0x1_84FF  frame_counter
  0x1_8500-0x1_85FF  object_tracker                         `VP_TRACK
  0x1_8800-0x1_8BFF  symbol_overlay                         `VP_TRACK
Interrupts: intc source 12 = isp_stats frame done (configure it as an
edge source), 13 = end of frame at the first pipeline stage, 14 = end of
frame at the last stage (frame_counter STATUS, level: write 1 to clear),
15 spare (ext_irq_i).

Configuration (src/configuration.sv): `VP_CSI2_RX, `VP_HDMI, `VP_LVDS,
`VP_DSI, `VP_CSI2_TX select the external video interfaces, `VP_VISION
adds vision_system, `VP_FILTER blur_sharpen and `VP_TRACK object_tracker
with symbol_overlay, all in the video_pipeline insert loop (`VP_INSERT,
enabled by CTRL[7]):
  insert point -> [vs_stream_adapter -> vision_system] -> [blur_sharpen]
    -> [object_tracker (tap) -> symbol_overlay] -> back
With vision_system in the path, keep CTRL.LOCK (genlock) set: there is
no frame buffer to repeat a frame, so each display frame waits in
vertical blanking for the next corrected frame (the display follows
vision_system's output rate, up to LOCK_MAX extra lines). vision_system
frames are at most 720 x 720 (barrel_pkg).

Clocks (defaults; see docs/clock_diagram.svg): ref_clk, the board
oscillator, 33.333 MHz (REF_KHZ). py_soc's clock generator makes
  cpu_clk      = ref x CPU_M / (CPU_D x CPU_O) = x24 / 4 = 200 MHz
                 (CPU PLL oscillator 800 MHz), CPU and peripherals
and, from cpu_clk (video PLL oscillator cpu_clk x VID_M / VID_D = x35
= 7 GHz, phase-aligned outputs):
  pix_clk      = / PIX_O  (70) = 100 MHz, core logic: video pipeline,
                 registers, vision_system, blur_sharpen, SDRAM
  tmds_ser_clk = / TMDS_O (7)  = 1 GHz, 10x pix_clk (HDMI 1 Gbit/s)
  lvds_ser_clk = / LVDS_O (10) = 700 MHz, 7x pix_clk (single link;
                 dual link 3.5x: LVDS_O = 20)
  tx_byte_clk  = / TXB_O  (56) = 125 MHz, D-PHY TX (1 Gbit/s per lane)
byte_clk (D-PHY RX) is recovered from the camera clock lane: an input.
SYSCTL CLK_EN gates each video clock (reset value CLK_EN_RST: core and
MIPI byte clocks on, the display serial clocks off until the firmware's
video set-up turns them on). CPU peripherals, one parameter set per
instance: UART0 console / UART1 host 115200 baud, I2C0 camera CCI
400 kHz, I2C1 DDC / EEPROM 100 kHz, SPI0 panel / touch 10 MHz, SPI1
ADC / sensors 2 MHz, boot flash 33 MHz (FLASH_CLKDIV 3); FIFOs 16 words.
For synthesis the PLL oscillators (dpll_dco) are black boxes: replace
them, or clk_gen, with the device PLL / MMCM.
Reset: arst_n, external, asynchronous active low, resets the CPU system
(py_soc, held until its CPU PLL locks). Its release starts the boot:
py_boot loads the firmware from flash, the firmware tests the CPU
peripherals and then releases the core logic reset by writing SYSCTL
CORE_RESET (py_soc core_rst_n_o, only while the video PLL is locked).
Until then every other block (video_pipeline, vision_system,
blur_sharpen, frame_counter, serializers) is held in reset: their only
reset is the CPU system's reset output core_rst_n_o, synchronised per
clock domain (reset_sync). arst_n reaches them through the CPU: it
resets py_soc, which clears CORE_RESET (one cpu_clk edge later).
core_rst_n_o shows the released state to the board. The watchdog resets
the CPU (wdt_reset_o shows it), which clears CORE_RESET and so puts the
core logic back into reset until the firmware has booted again.
```

## 7. Clocks, resets, clock-domain crossings and performance

- Clocks: `ref_clk`, `byte_clk`.
- Resets: `arst_n`; one `reset_sync` per domain.
- Resources: Last Yosys result: about 45550 LUTs, 618 DSP48E1, 15 RAMB36E1, 46 RAMB18E1.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 8. Control processor and firmware

Firmware `sw/camera.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware: the camera module.

Camera control over I2C 0 (CCI registers of the sensor at SENSOR_ADDR): the frame gap, the frame
size and the image name of the tracking sequence and "stream on"; the image format pin GPIO0[30] and the ISP set for it.
```

Firmware `sw/events.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware: the frame event transcript.

frame_counter logs every frame marker of the enabled channels in the order the markers happened,
time-stamped in microseconds (hardware: the order and the times are exact even when the report
falls behind). The channels follow a frame through the pipeline:
  0  end of frame out of csi2_raw_unpack, the first stage (interrupt 13, COUNT0)
  2  vision_system takes the frame (vs_stream_adapter admitted it)
  3  vision_system starts sending the corrected frame
  4  object_tracker has measured the frame (after blur_sharpen)
  1  end of frame into axis_to_video, the last stage (interrupt 14, COUNT1)
event_next() reports the oldest event as one line, "  [<time> us] <what happened>", so the UART 0
transcript is the true sequence of events. Interrupts 13 / 14 are serviced as they come (isr reads
COUNT0 / COUNT1); their lines appear in the transcript at the time the frame ended.
```

Firmware `sw/overlay.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware: symbol_overlay, the dashed tracking box and the text.

Object 0 is the tracking box: a 1-pixel dashed green rectangle (dashes of 4) TRK_PAD pixels outside
the target. Texts (3 x 5 font, on a darkened backdrop): T_NAME the image name in the upper left
corner, T_CLOCK a clock (time since the core logic started, HH:MM:SS.mmm) in the upper right, T_FRAME
"frame number <n>" in the lower left, the number counted by the overlay itself at every frame start
(exact on every frame). Changes are committed (overlay_commit), so they apply whole at the next
frame start.
```

Firmware `sw/search.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware: object_tracker search windows.

The tracker looks for the target only inside its search window (inclusive, taken at each frame
start): the whole frame while searching, else the predicted box plus TRK_MARGIN pixels.
```

Firmware `sw/sequence.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware: frame counters and the image sequence (section 7).

Once the pipeline is idle every frame count is cleared and the event log started on all channels,
so the camera's image sequence (GPIO0[29] = 1) is counted from 0 and every frame is followed
through the pipeline in the transcript: first stage (interrupt 13), into and out of
vision_system, measured by object_tracker, last stage (interrupt 14).
```

Firmware `sw/tracker.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware: object_tracker set-up and the tracking state machine.

States: SEARCH (whole frame), TRACK (target found: window around the prediction), COAST (target
missed: the box keeps moving with the velocity), back to SEARCH after TRK_LOST misses in a row.
Centres and velocities are kept x 2 (x0 + x1) and the box size grows at once but shrinks by a
quarter of the difference per frame, so everything is adds and shifts (py_core has no multiply or
divide). pred_lo / pred_hi give the predicted box for the next frame.
```

Firmware `sw/tracking.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware: pedestrian tracking (section 8).

The tracking sequence's frame size comes from the camera (registers 0x30-0x33) and is set in
every block; the tracker searches the whole frame and symbol_overlay waits for a target. The
transcript logs the first stage, the tracker and the last stage of every frame; on each tracker
event (track_event) the firmware reads the measurement, runs the state machine (tracker.py), moves
the dashed box (overlay.py) and the search window (search.py) to the predicted position for the
next frame, and completes the event's line with the result.
```

Firmware `sw/video_dump.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware: the video register dump (section 5).

Every register of video_pipeline, its scaler, vision_system, blur_sharpen, frame_counter,
object_tracker and symbol_overlay with a short description (dump() in video_init.py).
```

Firmware `sw/video_init.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware, part 1: py_soc CPU initialisation (library).

Imported by video_proc.py (the program; pyc.py inlines this file at its
"from video_init import *"). Everything here concerns the control CPU only:

  - the py_soc address map and peripheral register offsets;
  - text output on UART 0: putc, puts / say (strings from the flash string
    table, read through the flash controller), dec, hex32, result (one
    [PASS] / [FAIL] line, counted in passes / errors), heading;
  - cpu_isr(pending): the CPU's own interrupt sources (software interrupt,
    GPIO2 edge, watchdog pre-timeout), called by the program's handler;
  - cpu_init(start): report section 1 (boot-up sequence: reset cause, the
    boot image header read back from flash, boot status, SoC ID, start-up
    cycle count) and section 2 (peripheral self-test, one PASS / FAIL line
    each: system control, interrupt controller, GPIO loopback and edge
    interrupt, UART 1 / UART 0 loopback, SPI 0 / SPI 1 loopback, I2C 0
    camera control registers, I2C 1 EEPROM, SPI flash, watchdog);
  - section 3 (CPU register dump): every CPU peripheral register with a
    short description (skipped when the GPIO0[31] quick-simulation strap is
    high);
  - the last step of cpu_init: after a successful boot (every self-test
    passed) the core logic reset is released by writing SYSCTL CORE_RESET;
    the logic outside the CPU (the video datapath) is held in reset until
    then, and stays there when a self-test failed;
  - dump(), reg_line(), dump_port(): register dump helpers.

The interrupt handler must be installed (irq_handler) before cpu_init: the
self-test waits for interrupts.
```

Firmware `sw/video_proc.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware: the program (interrupt handler and main).

Compiled with ip/cpu/py_core/tools/pyc.py into one flash image (scripts/run_sim.sh does it; pyc.py
inlines every module imported below, each once, into one global namespace); the py_soc boot loader
copies it from SPI flash at reset. Modules (sw/):
  video_init.py   CPU initialisation, peripheral self-test, text output on UART 0 (sections 1-3)
  video_regs.py   addresses, register offsets and bit values of the video blocks
  camera.py       camera control over I2C 0 (frame gap, frame size, stream on), image format pin
  video_setup.py  frame_size(), video set-up (section 4), video start (section 6)
  video_dump.py   video register dump (section 5)
  events.py       the frame event transcript from frame_counter's event log (true order, times)
  sequence.py     frame counters and image sequence (section 7)
  search.py       object_tracker search windows
  tracker.py      object_tracker set-up and the SEARCH / TRACK / COAST state machine
  overlay.py      symbol_overlay: the dashed tracking box
  tracking.py     pedestrian tracking (section 8) Every step
is reported on UART 0 as readable text (the testbench saves it to
cpu_bootup.txt):

  1.-3. CPU initialisation (video_init.py): boot-up sequence, CPU
     peripheral self-test, CPU register dump. The external reset holds the
     whole system; its release starts the CPU boot, while the core logic
     (video datapath) stays in reset until the CPU, having booted and passed
     its self-test, releases it (SYSCTL CORE_RESET). Without that release
     (a self-test failed) the video sections are skipped.
  4. Video set-up, every video register programmed with the camera still
     stopped: display serial clocks on (SYSCTL CLK_EN), camera out of
     reset (GPIO0[0]), camera frame gap (end of one frame to the start of
     the next, FRAME_GAP_NS = 1280 ns, CCI registers
     0x20-0x21 over I2C 0), vision_system identity correction, blur_sharpen
     MODE 3, video_pipeline with the insert point, image format, frame
     counter and statistics interrupts.
     The camera image format comes from the GPIO0[30] input (1 = monochrome:
     every ISP stage bypassed, the raw value on R, G and B; 0 = colour: RGGB
     demosaic on). An interrupt on either edge reprograms the ISP BYPASS
     register (set_format, applied by the ISP at the next frame start) and
     GPIO0[2] shows the format programmed.
  5. Video register dump: video_pipeline, its scaler, vision_system,
     blur_sharpen and frame_counter, with a short description (skipped when
     the GPIO0[31] strap is high: quick simulation).
  6. Video start: camera "stream on" over I2C 0, frames, checks.
  7. Frame counters and image sequence: frame_counter counts the ends of
     frame of the first pipeline stage (csi2_raw_unpack, interrupt 13,
     COUNT0) and of the last one (into axis_to_video, interrupt 14, COUNT1);
     the interrupt handler reads the respective counter at each one. Once
     the pipeline is idle every count and the event log are cleared, so the
     image sequence (GPIO0[29] = 1) is counted from 0, and every frame is
     followed through the pipeline in the transcript, one line per event in
     the order the events happened, with its time (frame_counter's event
     log, events.py): first stage (IRQ 13, COUNT0), into and out of
     vision_system, measured by object_tracker, last stage (IRQ 14, COUNT1).
  8. Pedestrian tracking: the camera's frame size for the tracking
     sequence is read from its control registers 0x30-0x33 (width, height,
     high byte first, over I2C 0) and every block is reprogrammed for it
     (frame_size), object_tracker searches the whole frame for a dark
     object, and symbol_overlay draws a dashed box around it. For every
     frame of the camera's tracking sequence (GPIO0[29] = 1 again) the
     transcript shows the first stage, the tracker and the last stage; at
     the tracker event the firmware reads the tracker's box, predicts where
     the pedestrian will be in the next frame (centre velocity, shifts
     only: no multiply or divide in py_core), moves the dashed box and the
     search window there and completes the line with the result. States: SEARCH (whole frame),
     TRACK (window around the prediction), COAST (target missed, box
     keeps moving with the velocity), back to SEARCH after TRK_LOST misses.
  9. Summary and "END OF REPORT".

Text lives in a string table in flash (pyc.py: a string literal is a handle);
puts() reads it through the flash controller. The testbench watches the
`stage`, `errors` and `frames` globals: stage 3 = CPU initialised, 100 = video
running, 160 = frame-count report, 161 = waiting for the image sequence, 170 = tracking
set up (waiting for the tracking sequence), 180 = tracking report, 200 = done.
```

Firmware `sw/video_regs.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware: addresses, register offsets and bit values of the video blocks.

Every module of the firmware imports this file (pyc.py inlines it once); the values are
compile-time constants, folded by pyc.py.
```

Firmware `sw/video_setup.py`:

```text
video_processor firmware: video set-up (section 4) and video start (section 6).

frame_size() sets one frame size everywhere (camera input, vision_system, blur_sharpen,
object_tracker, display active area); video_setup() programs every video register with the camera
stopped; video_start() turns the camera on and checks that frames flow.
```

## 9. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; iverilog 12+, Verilator lint clean, Yosys (sv2v where needed); AXI4-Stream for data, AXI4-Lite for control; honour back-pressure.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).

## 10. File header

Read the file header template from `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt` and start every file you create (RTL, testbench, test tasks, scripts, file lists, Makefile) with that header, filled in: Filename, Author: FPGA Cores 4 U, Description, Date. In RTL the Description is the specification (behaviour, register map, parameters, clocks, resets, clock-domain crossings, latency, resources, errors); in testbenches it says what is checked; test-task files list every task with a one-line description (the test list scripts use it).

Header template file: `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt`   (replace with your own template file if needed)

## 11. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Tools

Use these tools for each step (the selection lives in `ip/.tools`; keep every script working with the default tools):

| Step | Tool | How it is run |
|------|------|---------------|
| Simulation | Icarus Verilog (`iverilog -g2012`, `vvp`) | `make test` / `scripts/run_sim.sh`; alternatives VCS, ModelSim, Questa (`SIMULATOR` in `ip/.tools`) |
| Python (cocotb) tests | cocotb on Verilator | `make python-test` (`PYTHON_SIMULATOR`) |
| Lint | Verilator (`--lint-only -Wall`) | `run_sim.sh --lint` (systems: `make lint`) |
| Waveform viewing | Surfer (VCD) | `make wave` / `run_sim.sh --wave` (`--vcd` only dumps) |
| Code coverage | Verilator `--coverage` + `verilator_coverage`, `ip/tools/cov/cov_report.py` | `make cov` / `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh` (LCOV `coverage.info`; vendor simulators: native coverage) |
| Formatting | `ip/scripts/sv_format.py` | `--check` before delivery |
| Synthesis | Yosys (Xilinx 7-series flow, sv2v where needed) | `make synth`; alternative Synplify (`SYNTHESIS`) |
| Place and route (optional) | Vivado | `PLACE_ROUTE` in `ip/.tools`, once a device is chosen |
| Diagrams | Graphviz (`dot`) | `make diagram` / `make diagrams` |
| Firmware (py_soc) | Python 3 + `ip/cpu/py_core/tools/pyc.py` | run by `scripts/run_sim.sh` |
| Test list | `ip/scripts/list_tests.py` | `run_sim.sh --list-tests` / `make list-tests` |
| Prompts and docs | `make_ip_prompts.py`, `gen_docs.py`, `make_block_diagrams.py` | regenerate after a change |

## 14. Verification

The reference design is verified as follows; cover at least the same:

```text
tb/video_processor_tb.sv:
System testbench of video_processor. Nothing is programmed
by the testbench: py_soc boots the firmware (sw/video_proc.py with the
CPU initialisation sw/video_init.py, compiled by pyc.py) from a SPI flash model
and the firmware brings the system up over its external AXI4-Lite
window, reporting every step on UART 0. Reset: arst_n (external) resets
the CPU system; the core logic (video) stays in reset until the CPU has
booted, passed its self-test and written SYSCTL CORE_RESET
(core_rst_n_o, checked by test_core_reset). Board models:
  - spi_flash_bfm holding the firmware image and string table (pyc.py);
  - camera module: sensor CCI register model (i2c_bfm, address
    0x36 on I2C 0) and a CSI-2 RAW10 source (csi2_bfm) that
    streams 32x24 frames only after the firmware releases its reset
    (GPIO0[0]) and writes "stream on" (register 0x01 = 1);
  - I2C EEPROM (i2c_bfm, 0x50 on I2C 1); UART, SPI and GPIO
    looped back (txd -> rxd, MOSI -> MISO, gpio_o -> gpio_i) for the
    firmware's peripheral self-test; GPIO0[31] = +quick strap (the
    firmware then skips the register dumps); GPIO0[30] = image
    format pin (1 monochrome, 0 colour; the firmware reprograms the ISP
    on each change and shows the result on GPIO0[2]); GPIO0[29] = image
    sequence running;
  - UART 0 receiver: decodes the report at UART_BAUD, writes it to
    cpu_bootup.txt and echoes each line as "UART0| ...";
  - HDMI: tmds_serializer lanes deserialised on the TMDS clock lane and
    decoded by hdmi_bfm; LVDS link A deserialised on the clock
    lane and decoded as single-link VESA 24 bpp. Their serial clocks and
    the camera stop after the video checks (the report runs on);
  - image test: 4 colour and 4 monochrome images (frame_c_<n>_input.ppm,
    frame_m_<n>_input.ppm in input_images/, generated when missing) are
    sent by the camera (colour as a Bayer RGGB mosaic) one frame each.
    The camera paces the sequence so every image flows through the
    whole pipeline: the next image starts once vision_system has taken
    the previous one and can take another (vs_stream_adapter would
    otherwise drop it), and never sooner than the camera's frame gap
    (CCI registers 0x20-0x21, ns from the end of one frame to the start
    of the next, power-on value 1280, programmed by the firmware); the
    format pin for the next image changes as soon as the previous
    frame's last line is sent. The firmware clears both frame counters
    once the pipeline is idle, so the sequence is counted from 0 (one
    frame sent: count 1, all 8 images: 8 at both stages); it reports
    every end of frame on UART 0 (counts 1, 2, 3, ... at each stage).
    The frame of each image at the output of every
    module (csi2_raw_unpack .. isp_csc, vision_system, blur_sharpen, HDMI,
    LVDS) is saved as output_images/<module>_<c|m>_<n>_output.ppm (P6).
    Frames are labelled on their way through the pipeline.
    Plusargs: +IMG_IN_DIR=<dir>, +IMG_OUT_DIR=<dir>.
  - pedestrian tracking: an animated GIF (gif_io reader; default
    tb/images/pedestrian_walk.gif, 128 x 96 black-and-white street
    video of a pedestrian, 50 frames = 5 s, made by
    tb/scripts/make_pedestrian_gif.py) sets the tracking frame size: the
    GIF's own (width a multiple of 4, height even, scaled down to fit
    320 x 240), loaded at start-up into the camera's control registers
    0x30-0x33 (width, height, high byte first), which the firmware reads
    over I2C 0 to reprogram every block (stage 170), and its base name
    into registers 0x40-0x4F (the overlay's upper-left text). The camera then sends
    one RAW10 frame per GIF frame; GPIO0[29] is high while it lasts.
    The frames at the tracker input (after blur_sharpen), at the
    overlay output and on HDMI are captured, with each frame's overlay
    settings, tracker window and results; the HDMI frames are written
    as an animated GIF with the input's frame times (gif_io writer;
    gif-output/<input name>_tracked.gif) and read back. LVDS
    is checked before this and its serial clock is stopped for it.
    Plusargs: +GIF_IN=<file> (any animated GIF),
    +GIF_BW (convert a colour GIF to black and white; otherwise it is
    sent in colour as an RGGB mosaic), +GIF_DIR=<dir> (GIF outputs,
    default gif-output), +GIF_IN_DIR=<dir> (the input sequence as sent,
    default gif-input), +GIF_OUT=<file>, +GIF_FRAMES=<n>
    (send only the first n frames, a shorter run).
The test tasks are in tests/video_processor_tests.sv (`included).
Prints TEST PASSED on success.
```

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `scripts/run_sim.sh --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `video_processor_tb` | `test_boot` | py_soc boots the firmware (sw/video_proc.py) from the SPI flash model (boot_done, no boot error). |
| `video_processor_tb` | `test_core_reset` | the core logic (video) stays in reset while the CPU boots and tests its peripherals, and leaves it only when the CPU writes SYSCTL CORE_RESET after a clean initialisation (stage 3, no errors). |
| `video_processor_tb` | `test_firmware` | the firmware reaches stage 100 (video running) with no errors (its CPU peripheral self-test included), counted >= 6 isp_stats interrupts and switched the "running" LED (GPIO0[1]) on. |
| `video_processor_tb` | `test_vision_output` | vision_system's output (csi2_rx -> ISP bypassed: raw / 4 on R, G, B -> insert point -> vs_stream_adapter -> identity correction) is the camera image within 1 LSB (vision_system's own tolerance) and the same in every frame. |
| `video_processor_tb` | `test_hdmi` | the HDMI image (tmds_serializer lanes deserialised and decoded by hdmi_bfm) equals it exactly; no HDMI protocol error. |
| `video_processor_tb` | `test_lvds` | the LVDS link A image (VESA 24 bpp) equals it exactly. |
| `video_processor_tb` | `test_adapter` | vision_system processed frames and lost no corrected pixel (return FIFO). |
| `video_processor_tb` | `test_uart_report` | the UART 0 report (saved to cpu_bootup.txt) reaches "END OF REPORT" with no [FAIL] line and at least MIN_PASS [PASS] lines, and the firmware stage is 200. The frame event transcript ("  [<time> us] <event>" lines) is the true sequence: every line is the next marker frame_counter logged (channel, count and time, in the order the testbench saw the markers), counts run 1, 2, 3, ... per channel, times never go back, each frame's events come before its last-stage end; every image of the sequence is reported at all 5 points (section 7) and every GIF frame at the first stage, the tracker and the last stage (section 8). |
| `video_processor_tb` | `test_images` | 4 colour and 4 monochrome images, one frame each, paced so each image reaches vision_system (the next one starts once vision_system can take it, at least the camera's frame gap later; the camera sets the image format pin GPIO0[30] during the gap before each image; the firmware reprograms the ISP). Each image's frame at every module output it reached is saved as output_images/<module>_<c/m>_<n>_output.ppm. Checks: monochrome - the ISP output (isp_csc) is the input image exactly; colour - the demosaic keeps every native Bayer sample and the output is in colour; both - vision_system within 1 LSB of isp_csc, blur_sharpen equals conv2d_ref of vision_system, HDMI and LVDS equal blur_sharpen. Every image must pass the whole pipeline (none dropped by vs_stream_adapter). frame_counter: both counts 0 before the sequence (cleared by the firmware), then 8 at the first and 8 at the last stage. |
| `video_processor_tb` | `test_tracking` | pedestrian tracking: the input GIF (+GIF_IN, any animated GIF; default the pedestrian, 128 x 96, 50 frames) is read with gif_io at start-up; its size (fitted to 320 x 240) is the frame size the firmware reads from the camera (registers 0x30-0x33) and programs everywhere. A colour GIF is sent in colour (RGGB mosaic, ISP demosaic), or converted to black and white with +GIF_BW (also written as gif-input/<name>_bw.gif; the sequence as sent is written to gif-input/<name>_<w>x<h>.gif). Once the firmware has set every block to that size (stage 170) the camera sends each GIF frame (paced like the image test, GPIO0[29] high). Checks per frame: the object_tracker results equal track_ref's model of its input frame and window; the symbol_overlay output equals the model's drawing of the objects it applied; the HDMI image equals the overlay output. Tracking: the pedestrian is found in the first frame (whole-frame search) and from the second frame on object 0 is an enabled dashed rectangle containing the centre of the true figure (track_ref find_dark on the GIF frame) and, from the third, covering at least 75 % of it; the firmware counted every frame as found. (Quality is judged only on frames with a dark target, so any GIF can be used.) The HDMI frames are written as an animated GIF (+GIF_OUT, input frame times) and read back within 1 grey level. frame_counter counted every GIF frame. |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

## 15. Report back

Files created, block, clock and reset diagrams, address map, every change to existing IP and why, decisions for missing functions, the test list with results (with a mutation check), coverage per metric (and every waiver), synthesis utilisation, known limits.
